questions.q: What is the main problem with naively padding every short document up to the model's full context length?
options: It makes the tokenizer vocabulary too large
Padding tokens carry no training signal but still cost full attention compute, wasting a large fraction of GPU time
It causes the model to memorize padding tokens as real words
It increases the vocabulary size automatically
questions.explain: A short document padded to a much longer fixed sequence length can be mostly padding tokens, which produce no useful gradient yet still cost the same attention compute as real content.

questions.q: What does sequence packing do instead of padding?
options: It deletes short documents entirely from the training set
It concatenates multiple documents end-to-end, separated by an EOS token, then chunks the result into fixed-length sequences
It converts short documents into images
It duplicates short documents until they reach the target length
questions.explain: Packing concatenates many documents into one long token stream and splits that stream into fixed-length blocks, so nearly every position in a training sequence carries real content instead of padding.

questions.q: Which Hugging Face `trl` feature implements the same concatenate-and-chunk packing pattern described in this lesson?
options: AutoModelForCausalLM
ConstantLengthDataset / packing=True on SFTTrainer
BpeTrainer
MinHashLSH
questions.explain: trl's ConstantLengthDataset and the packing=True option on SFTTrainer implement the concatenate-and-chunk packing pattern for fine-tuning data.

questions.q: What is the 'cross-document attention problem' that packing introduces?
options: Tokens from two unrelated documents in the same packed sequence can attend to each other under standard causal attention, which is semantically meaningless
Packed sequences cannot use any attention mechanism at all
Packing always removes the EOS token, making documents indistinguishable
The vocabulary size doubles whenever packing is used
questions.explain: Because packed sequences concatenate unrelated documents, a token near the start of one document can, under standard causal attention, attend across the boundary into a prior unrelated document -- a semantically meaningless signal.

questions.q: How does a document-aware, block-diagonal attention mask address the cross-document attention problem?
options: It removes the need for tokenization entirely
It restricts each token's attention to only tokens from the same original document within the packed sequence
It increases the context length automatically
It forces every document to be padded instead of packed
questions.explain: A block-diagonal mask only allows a token to attend to other tokens that came from the same source document, fully preventing cross-document attention leakage within a packed sequence.
